clue.text: Duenna takes in art-master as interpreter

indicators.note: takes in says the chaperone's word swallows the master's letters inside it

parts.note: a duenna is a fierce chaperone, a dragon
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A Spanish chaperone brings along an art teacher to translate for her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes in' is the container signal. A dragon is crossword shorthand for a stern female chaperone, which is exactly what a Spanish duenna was.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman is a guide and translator in Arabic-, Turkish- or Persian-speaking lands.

clue.text: Take part in practice

parts.note: read as going over one's part in a practice session before the real performance

explanation.surface: Join in a training session.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through a play's lines or a piece of music in a practice run before performing it.

clue.text: Philosopher takes Jane to the old mountain

parts.note: William Godwin was an English political philosopher

explanation.surface: A thinker goes walking with a famous novelist up an old peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' simply joins the two surnames. Mount Godwin-Austen was the old name for K2, the world's second-highest peak, after the surveyor Henry Godwin-Austen.
explanation.definitionFit: K2 in the Karakoram was formerly named after the surveyor who mapped it, so the name belongs to an old mountain title.

clue.text: Curses girl for interrupting writer's work

indicators.note: interrupting says the girl's name breaks into the middle of the writer's work

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, what a writer produces

explanation.surface: A young woman's interruptions spoil an author's work and draw oaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Malison is an archaic word for a curse or malediction, so the plural means curses.

clue.text: Book to see actor

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A suggestion to read a book to get a look at a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Novello was a Welsh actor, composer and matinee idol of the British stage and screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello was a celebrated stage and film performer between the wars.

clue.text: Buy it back ? Think again !

definitions.meaning: to purchase something back, as from a pawnbroker
split as ..., to judge or consider once more

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over repurchasing something they sold.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover a pawned item by paying is the usual sense; read as re-deem it means to judge anew.

clue.text: Miss Verity losing her head ?

indicators.note: losing her head says the first letter of the synonym is cut off

explanation.surface: A young woman named Verity seems to have lost her composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss Verity' looks like a person's name, but 'Miss' is the definition (a girl's name) and 'Verity' is wordplay for TRUTH, which loses its head T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a girl's given name, so it can stand for an unmarried young woman addressed as Miss.

clue.text: Retaliation concerning Paris trip, many conclude

indicators.note: conclude says the piece for many comes at the very end
the city's name trips and stumbles, so its letters fall into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number

explanation.surface: Revenge over a trip to Paris, as many people decide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' is the anagram signal on the city, and 'conclude' sends the Roman fifty, a crossword stand-in for many, to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is an act of revenge or retaliation for an injury.

clue.text: Proposal is noted ?

parts.note: an opening offer in negotiation, which in music is also a piece written in notes, played before an opera

explanation.surface: A suggestion has been recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is an approach or offer made to open talks, and also the orchestral introduction to an opera.

clue.text: Such a deep part of the lake !

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at how deep one stretch of a lake is.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Chad is a large shallow lake in Africa, so the exclamation is ironic.
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a large freshwater lake on the edge of the Sahara.

clue.text: Come safely through without strike, eh ? That's lucky

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the survival word wraps round the rest

parts.note: to weather a storm is to come safely through it

explanation.surface: Getting through unscathed without a walkout, isn't that fortunate?
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, the container signal. A sprig of white heather is a Scottish good-luck token.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig of white heather is traditionally carried for good fortune, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Sport occupies four nights — it appears wrong

indicators.note: wrong says these letters are set out in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A game takes up four evenings and seems mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges FOUR NIGHTS IT; 'occupies' and 'appears' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Angling for trout is a field sport practised on rivers and lakes.

clue.text: Rob irregular soldier 'of horse

indicators.note: irregular says the letters of rob are put out of their usual order

parts.note: an NCO is a non-commissioned officer, a soldier

explanation.surface: Steal an irregular fighter's horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' looks like it describes the soldier, but it is the anagram signal on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronco is an unbroken or half-tamed horse of the American West.

clue.text: Current content of divers satires

indicators.note: content of says the electrical piece is the contents sitting inside the birds

parts.note: an amp is a unit of electric current

explanation.surface: An electric current runs through what various satirists write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' looks like the old word for various, but it is the diving birds, LOONS, which hold AMP: L-AMP-OONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lampoons are satirical attacks that ridicule a person in writing or verse.

clue.text: There's some point in backing issues for Moslems

indicators.note: in says the compass point sits inside the turned word
backing means the word issues is read from back to front

parts.note: N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Some see the point in supporting the issues raised by Muslims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns ISSUES into SEUSSI, and 'in' puts N into it: SE-N-USSI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Senussi are a Muslim religious order and tribe of Libya.

clue.text: Employees take the ring road in town

explanation.surface: Workers drive the ring road around town.
explanation.walkthrough: Stafford is the county town of Staffordshire in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Stafford is an English county town, in Staffordshire.

clue.text: After talk, permitted return: of property

indicators.note: after says the reversed piece follows the word for talk
return means the word for permitted is read backwards

explanation.surface: After a conversation, someone is allowed to get back their goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' fixes the order and 'return' is the reversal signal; the colon in the held text is not in the printed clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A chattel is an item of movable personal possession, as opposed to land.

clue.text: Old general went over the range

definitions.text: Old general went over the range

parts.words: Old general went over the range
parts.note: the Carthaginian commander who crossed the Alps with elephants to invade Italy

explanation.surface: A veteran commander crossed the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Carthaginian general famously crossed the Alps in 218 BC to attack Rome.

clue.text: A garden farewell to un toothsome creatures

parts.note: Eden is the garden of Genesis

explanation.surface: Goodbye to a garden of unappetising animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'un-toothsome' is split to mean toothless rather than unappetising; edentates such as anteaters and sloths lack front teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentata is the old zoological order of toothless or nearly toothless mammals such as sloths and armadillos.

clue.text: Gamble about girl upsetting the title

indicators.note: about says the bet goes round the other piece
upsetting in a down clue turns the girl's name upside down, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: A wager over a young woman ruins a noble rank.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upsetting' turns a word upside down, so it reads backwards; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet holds a hereditary British rank below a baron, the honour itself being a title.

clue.text: Nymph is heart-broken-goes to country

indicators.note: broken says the letters of heart are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A heartbroken nymph emigrates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart-broken' reads as grief-stricken, but 'broken' is the anagram signal on 'heart'; 'is' and 'goes to' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Arethusa was a nymph of Greek myth who became a spring to escape the river god Alpheus.

clue.text: Mysteriously haunts a French island

indicators.note: mysteriously says the letters of haunts are arranged in a puzzling new order

explanation.surface: Someone or something eerily frequents an island off France.
explanation.walkthrough: Ushant is the English name of Ouessant, off the tip of Brittany.
explanation.definitionFit: Ushant is an island off the north-west coast of Brittany.

clue.text: Notts, opener wasn't well caught

indicators.note: opener says to take the first letter of the county name

parts.note: ailed means was ill, wasn't well

explanation.surface: Nottinghamshire's opening batsman was off form and got caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: Notts is Nottinghamshire, an English county cricket side, and the opener is a cricket term too, but here it means just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail someone is to catch or arrest them.

clue.text: Shine in languages

explanation.surface: Someone excels at foreign tongues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shine' looks like a verb meaning excel, but it is the glossy finish of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: French polish is a shellac-based finish giving furniture a high gloss.

clue.text: Poetry has no opening in this tongue

indicators.note: has no opening says the first letter of the poetry word is removed

explanation.surface: Poems lack an introduction in this language.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: State gets coward's confession

definitions.meaning: a country in the Middle East
read as ..., what someone who fled would admit

explanation.surface: A nation receives an admission of cowardice.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a Middle Eastern nation; split as two words it is an admission of running away.

clue.text: Peer's son gives wrong answer

indicators.note: wrong says the letters are in the wrong order and need rearranging

parts.note: the letters of the word as printed, its S included

explanation.surface: A nobleman's son gives an incorrect reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges PEERS SON, the possessive S included.
explanation.definitionFit: A response is a reply or answer.

clue.text: Message from the border — permitted to return

indicators.note: return says the two pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: marge is a poetic word for margin or border

explanation.surface: A dispatch from the frontier says one may come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns MARGE LET into TEL EGRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram is a message sent by telegraph.
